title: Profile: Kelli Bourgeois, City Administrator of Oakdale
summary:
Oakdale's city administrator was hired, not elected, and she has been on the job about seven weeks. A factual portrait from the public record and her own words: what an appointed administrator actually is, the full hiring record behind her 5–0 appointment, the salary the public packet does not contain, thirty years of municipal work from South Dakota to Becker to Columbia Heights to Bristol, Tennessee — and what is on her desk in Oakdale right now.

THE OFFICE: The city administrator is described by the city as "the chief administrative officer for the City of Oakdale," managing administrative processes and carrying out council policy; the administration department also covers communications, information technology and licensing. The council cited Oakdale's code of ordinances (Ch. 2, Art. 3, Sec. 2-34) and Minn. Stat. § 412.111, which lets a council appoint officers, "prescribe the duties and fix the compensation" of them, and remove an appointed officer when, in its judgment, "the public welfare will be promoted by the removal." No term, no election. Oakdale's elected five: Mayor Kevin Zabel and council members Kari Moore, Andy Morcomb, Gary Severson and Katie Wrich.

HOW SHE GOT IT: Outgoing City Administrator Chris Volkers, who had served the city since June 2020, announced her intent to retire by June 30, 2026. The city hired search firm MGT on Nov. 25, 2025 after reviewing ten proposals; the job posted in late December; applications closed Feb. 6, 2026. Mayor Zabel told the April 14 meeting the search drew about 70 applicants; the council interviewed five finalists at a special workshop on March 26, 2026 (9 a.m.–6:45 p.m.) and chose Bourgeois that day. The council approved the appointment and employment agreement 5–0 on April 14, 2026. She became a city employee June 16 and city administrator June 22; Volkers stayed through June 30.

THE SALARY: Not in the public packet. The city's staff report says the signed agreement went to council members under separate nonpublic cover "as it is nonpublic data under Minn. Stat. Sec. 13.43, subd. 4, until it is fully executed by her and the City." A resident who wants the figure should request the executed agreement from the city.

WHO SHE IS: More than 30 years of municipal experience, per the city's staff report; B.A. in local and urban affairs, St. Cloud State University; J.D., Hamline University School of Law; ICMA Credentialed Manager. Senior planner, South Eastern Council of Governments, Sioux Falls, S.D. (~4 years); 16 years in Becker, Minn.; Columbia Heights from 2014 as HR director and assistant city manager, then city manager from January 2019; city manager of Bristol, Tenn., April 2023 to June 3, 2026.

ON HER DESK: A two-person bond pricing committee (city administrator and finance director) created by Resolution 2026-35 at her first regular meeting, June 23, 2026, with authority to approve the Series 2026A general obligation bond sale — street reconstruction plus the police expansion and city hall remodel — scheduled for Aug. 13, 2026. A rewrite of the municipal vehicle policy into a take-home vehicle policy. A proposed survey of the city's citizen advisory bodies feeding the council's strategic planning. Inherited: the police expansion and city hall remodel (April 14 council approval of a $7,940,489 guaranteed maximum price for Bid Package 2, Kraus-Anderson construction manager, 5–0) and the water filtration plant expansion tied to PFAS and 3M settlement funds.

SOURCES: City of Oakdale council packets at oakdalemn.gov/AgendaCenter — April 14, 2026 (_04142026-872), April 28, 2026 (_04282026-875, containing approved April 14 minutes), July 14, 2026 (_07142026-895, containing June 23 workshop and regular minutes), August 12, 2026 (_08122026-903, containing July 28 workshop minutes); City of Oakdale "Administration Department" page; Minnesota Statutes § 412.111 (revisor.mn.gov). Attributed secondary sources: MyNortheaster.com, "Bourgeois begins as Heights city manager" (career chronology and three quotes); WCYB (Bristol budget-adoption quote; resignation quotes and effective date); WJHL/Yahoo (combined Bristol FY2026 budget figure). Bristol's own budget document could not be retrieved — its host blocks automated access — and that limitation is stated on air.

TO VERIFY OR PARTICIPATE: The Oakdale City Council meets tonight, Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026 at 7 p.m. at the Discovery Center, 4444 Hadley Ave. N., with open forum limited to three minutes per person. Up for consideration: an HKGi professional services contract for the 2050 Comprehensive Plan update; playground bids for Tower Park and Golfview Park recommended to Pember Companies at $248,894.39; a cost-share agreement with Washington County for 34th Street North and High Point Drive; claims of $1,968,747.76; and two closed sessions on pending litigation from a city employee under Minn. Stat. § 13D.05, subd. 3(b), with a separation and release agreement in open session between them. None of it is decided until the council votes. Agendas, packets and minutes: oakdalemn.gov/AgendaCenter. Records requests, including the executed employment agreement, go to the City of Oakdale, 1584 Hadley Ave. N.
